arxiv-2302-11766.title: MUTANT : A Multi-sentential Code-mixed Hinglish Dataset
arxiv-2302-11766.creator: Rahul Gupta, Vivek Srivastava, Mayank Singh
arxiv-2302-11766.description: Abstract The multi-sentential long sequence textual data unfolds several interesting research directions pertaining to natural language processing and generation. Though we observe several high-quality long-sequence datasets for English and other monolingual languages, there is no significant effort in building such resources for code-mixed languages such as Hinglish (code-mixing of Hindi-English).

arxiv-2304-07767.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiang Li, Xi Cen, Zunwei Fu, Zhongci Hang. arxiv-2306-05161.creator: Anindya Basu, Indrani Kar
arxiv-2306-05161.description: Abstract This article investigates the resilient control problem for Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) with multiple sensors, where both sides of the communication channels are affected by Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks. While previous work focused on characterizing Multi-Channel DoS (MCDoS), this study emphasizes the characterization of Full-Scale DoS (FSDoS). First, a partial observer technique is proposed to address the MCDoS condition.

arxiv-2512-21261.description: Abstract This paper introduces a dynamic formulation of divergence-regularized optimal transport with weak targets on the path space. In our formulation, the classical relative entropy penalty is replaced by a general convex divergence, and terminal constraints are imposed in a weak sense.

europmc-pmc4389235.title: PD-1 alters T-cell metabolic reprogramming by inhibiting glycolysis and promoting lipolysis and fatty acid oxidation.
europmc-pmc4389235.creator: Patsoukis N, Bardhan K, Chatterjee P, Sari D, Liu B, Bell LN, Karoly ED, Freeman GJ, Petkova V, Seth P, Li L, Boussiotis VA.
europmc-pmc4389235.description: During activation, T cells undergo metabolic reprogramming, which imprints distinct functional fates. We determined that on PD-1 ligation, activated T cells are unable to engage in glycolysis or amino acid metabolism but have an increased rate of fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO)....

pmc-11657267.title: Spatial transcriptome profiling identifies DTX3L and BST2 as key biomarkers in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma tumorigenesis
pmc-11657267.creator: Rutao Li, Na Li, Qianqian Yang, Xing Tong, Wei Wang, Chang Li, Jun Zhao, Dong Jiang, Haitao Huang, Chen Fang, Kai Xie, Jiamin Yuan, Shaomu Chen, Guangbin Li, Haitao Luo, Zhibo Gao, Dongfang Wu, Xiaoli Cui, Wei Jiang, Lingchuan Guo, Haitao Ma, Yu Feng
pmc-11657267.description: BackgroundUnderstanding the stepwise progression of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is crucial for developing customized strategies for early detection and optimal clinical management. Herein, we aimed to unravel the transcriptional and immunologic alterations occurring during malignant transformation and identify clinically significant biomarkers of ESCC.

pmc-11698020.title: Accrual Suspensions in Seamless Phase II/III Trials: A Review of NRG Oncology Trials
pmc-11698020.creator: Chen Hu, Boris Freidlin, Edward L Korn
pmc-11698020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PURPOSEA phase II/III trial is a type of phase III trial that has embedded in it an intermediate phase II go/no-go decision as to whether to continue the accrual to the phase III sample size. We examine the design characteristics and experience of a well-defined set of National Cancer Institute phase II/III trials, with special emphasis on designed accrual suspensions while awaiting the data to become mature enough for the phase II analysis.

pmc-12389686.title: Latest Advances in Inhalable Dry Powder Bacteriophage Therapy for Pulmonary Infections
pmc-12389686.creator: David Encinas-Basurto, Patricia Dolores Martinez-Flores, Joselyn García, Marco Antonio Lopez-Mata, Gerardo García-González, Gerardo E Rodea, Basanth Babu Eedara, Heidi M Mansour, Josue Juarez, Jesus Perez-Gil
pmc-12389686.description: The concerning increase in respiratory infections that are resistant to multiple drugs has led to a growing interest in bacteriophage therapy as a potential alternative to conventional antibiotics. Effective phage delivery to the lungs, however, presents several formulation and stability issues, particularly for inhalation-based methods.

pmc-12586627.title: Effective in vivo RNA base editing via engineered cytidine deaminase APOBECs fused with PUF proteins
pmc-12586627.creator: Wenjian Han, Bo Yuan, Xiaojuan Fan, Weike Li, Yiting Yuan, Yuefang Zhang, Shu Wang, Shifang Shan, Markus Hafner, Zefeng Wang, Zilong Qiu
pmc-12586627.description: Base editing stands at the forefront of genetic engineering, heralding precise genetic modifications with broad implications. While CRISPR-based DNA and RNA base editing systems capitalize on sgRNA-guided specificity and diverse deaminase functionalities, the pursuit of efficient C-to-U RNA editing has been hampered by the inherent constraints of cytidine deaminases.

pmc-12652591.title: Mini-Basketball for Preschool and School-Aged Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-12652591.creator: Daniel González-Devesa, Rui Zhou, Markel Rico-González, Carlos D Gómez-Carmona, Luis Ceballos-Laita
pmc-12652591.description: Background: Although the participation of children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in team sports presents challenges, group-based physical activities could offer specific benefits for their core symptoms. Therefore, the aim of this systematic review was to analyze the benefits of mini-basketball for children with ASD. Methods: A systematic review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines and was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251144800).

pmc-12654179.title: Atypical Morphological Variations of the Sacrum in the Korean Population: A PMCT-Based 3D Reconstruction Study
pmc-12654179.creator: Jeong-Hyun Park, Eun-Seo Park, Jaeho Cho, Yu-Jin Choi, Hyung-Wook Kwon, Digud Kim, Yunil Choe, Goeun Lee, Kwang-Rak Park
pmc-12654179.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: The sacrum is formed by five fused vertebrae and connects the lumbar spine to the coccyx. It has four pairs of foramina for sacral nerves and shows important anatomical variations. This study aims to analyze the frequency of atypical sacral morphology in the Korean population using 3D reconstruction of postmortem computed tomography (PMCT) images, and to provide a systematic classification and morphological characterization.

pmc-12708973.title: Increased Risk of Hematologic Malignancy in Moderate to Severe Psoriasis in Relation to the Use of Systemic Immunosuppressants: A Nationwide Population-Based Matched Cohort Study
pmc-12708973.creator: Yu Ri Woo, Kyunghee Chae, Seowon Song, Subin Lee, Yu Jin Lee, Hoon Kang, Sukil Kim, Jung Eun Kim
pmc-12708973.description: BackgroundThe relationship between cancer and the use of systemic immunosuppressants in psoriasis treatment has not well established. The aim of this study was to evaluate the association between the systemic immunosuppressants used in the treatment for psoriasis and the risk of certain cancers in Korean patients with moderate to severe psoriasis.

pmc-12717861.title: Retrospective Single-Center Outcomes After a First Bimatoprost Sustained-Release Implant
pmc-12717861.creator: Collin T Olevson, Anthony P Mai, Justin A Schweitzer, John P Berdahl, Tanner J Ferguson
pmc-12717861.description: PurposeTo evaluate the long-term efficacy of the bimatoprost sustained-release (SR) implant focusing on time to additional intraocular pressure (IOP) lowering intervention and changes in medication burden and IOP, with subgroup analyses by lens status and prior trabecular meshwork (TM) procedures.

pmc-13056974.title: Low Fischer’s ratio is associated with increased mortality in patients with kidney failure
pmc-13056974.creator: Qianying Zhang, Mohamed E. Suliman, Abdul Rashid Qureshi, Fujia Guo, Dario Troise, Ricong Xu, Peter Bárány, Olof Heimbürger, Peter Stenvinkel, Bengt Lindholm
pmc-13056974.description: Metabolic changes in kidney failure, including an altered ratio of plasma branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) to aromatic amino acids (AAAs), also known as Fischer’s ratio (FR), could potentially affect survival. We analyzed associations of FR with mortality in patients with kidney failure.

pmc-13109094.title: Feasibility and acceptability of a sleep health intervention among adolescents in Ugandan schools: A prospective pilot intervention study
pmc-13109094.creator: Denis Ndekezi, Rebecca Kyomugisha, Betty Nyangoma, Prossy Namirembe, Beatrice Nanyonga, Aaron Nyaruhuma, Claudia Ateo, Calvin Robert Rutainama, Katherine A Thomas, Ratifah Batuusa, Benson Muhindo, Sheilah Kasabiiti, Connie Alezuyo, Nambusi Kyegombe, Chris Bonell, Daniel Michelson, Fiona C Baker, Fai
pmc-13109094.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Study ObjectivesThere is little research on sleep health interventions in Africa. We assessed the feasibility and acceptability of a tiered sleep health intervention among Ugandan adolescents. The intervention, delivered in two secondary schools, comprised universal components (sleep education sessions, structural changes to light, temperature and school-timings) plus targeted psychologist-delivered group cognitive behaviour therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) for students with moderate/severe insomnia (Insomnia Severity Index ≥15).MethodsFeasibility and acceptability were assessed through semi-structured interviews immediately after the intervention (T1) and 3 months later (T2)

pmc-13180093.title: Surgical Management of Charcot Neuroarthropathy Involving the Hindfoot and Midfoot: A Case Series
pmc-13180093.creator: Rajesh Simon, Ani Susan Abraham, Dennis P Jose, Pratik Vishavadia
pmc-13180093.description: Background:Charcot neuroarthropathy (CN) involving both the hindfoot and midfoot represents a severe form of the disease and is often associated with significant instability, deformity, and an increased risk of ulceration. Although early-stage midfoot CN may be managed conservatively, combined hindfoot-midfoot involvement typically necessitates complex surgical reconstruction.

pmc-13256154.title: Iterative Adaptations in a Physical Activity Program for Children with Autism: A Feasibility and Implementation Study
pmc-13256154.creator: Miriam Richter, Marie K. Taylor, Teresa Lindstedt, Annika Lundkvist Josenby, Olof Rask, Christine T. Ekdahl
pmc-13256154.description: Background: Children and adolescents with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) are generally more sedentary and engage less in physical activity (PA) than their peers. Despite increasing evidence of benefits, practical guidance on implementing adapted PA programs in real-world settings remains limited.

pmc-13393424.title: Effects of different exercise modalities on depressive symptom score changes in patients with type 2 diabetes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13393424.creator: Kezhi Wang, Wenjun Xu, Shouyang Cao, Yunxiao Liu
pmc-13393424.description: BackgroundType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major global public health challenge, and depressive symptoms are common among patients with T2DM. These symptoms may impair quality of life, self-management behaviors, glycemic control, and long-term prognosis. Exercise is a promising non-pharmacological strategy, but the comparative effects of different exercise modalities on depressive symptom scores remain unclear.

pmc-13491113.title: Lumbar Belt for Nonspecific Low Back Pain
pmc-13491113.creator: Laurent Grange, Paul Calmels, Yves-Marie Pers, Guillaume Laustriat, Valérie Wieczorek, Nassima Saih, Mathieu De-Sèze, Christelle Nguyen, Camille Daste, Isabelle Fayolle-Minon, Emmanuel Coudeyre, François Rannou
pmc-13491113.description: Key PointsQuestionDoes adding a nonrigid lumbar belt to usual care improve disability and pain in adults with nonspecific low back pain?FindingsIn this randomized clinical trial of 168 adults with nonspecific low back pain lasting 1 to 6 months, the belt group had greater improvement in Oswestry Disability Index at week 12 than usual care.

pmc-13658530.title: CT radiomics machine learning for predicting treatment response in unresectable stage III-IV NSCLC: insights from dual chemo-immunotherapy and immunotherapy cohorts
pmc-13658530.creator: Silvia Gigli, Lucia Malzone, Nicholas Landini, Roberta Valerieva Ninkova, Sandrine Riccardi, Giacomo Bonito, Laura Pappalardo, Alain Gelibter, Lucia Manganaro, Paolo Ricci
pmc-13658530.description: PurposeThe purpose of this study was to develop a machine learning model based on radiomic features extracted from baseline contrast-enhanced CT scans for predicting early treatment responses in two cohorts of patients with stage III-IV NSCLC treated with distinct therapeutic regimens (first-line chemo-immunotherapy or immunotherapy alone).
